data.name: Sidhu
data.gender_notes: Sidhu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who follows the Sidhas, or spiritual masters and seekers of enlightenment. The name Sidhu carries the meaning “Follower of the Sidhas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Punjabi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Sidhu usually hope their child will grow to embody follower of the sidhas and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sidhus are revered in Hinduism for their spiritual prowess and devotion to their gurus.
data.etymology: Sidhu belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Follower of the Sidhas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sidhu total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kumar" is popular in various regions of India and Nepal and is culturally associated with young boys or youths.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the term "Kumar" is also associated with Lord Subrahmanyan, who is considered a youthful god and the commander of all the serpents.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Sidhu is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Shidh' which means wise or intelligent. It is believed that individuals with this name possess deep inner wisdom and the ability to make insightful decisions. Sidhu also represents the divine aspect of knowledge and understanding.

historical_references.reference: Sidhu Kanhaiya was a renowned Sikh preacher and poet. He is believed to have lived during the late 16th or early 17th century. He is known for his devotional hymns in the Punjabi language, which express deep love and devotion towards God and Guru.

Sidhu Suraj was a famous Hindu warrior and king of the Sisodia Rajput clan. He ruled the Mewar kingdom during the late 13th and early 14th century. He is best known for his bravery during the siege of Chittorgarh fort, where he sacrificed his life rather than surrender to the invading army.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Sidhu continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Sidhu from Chennai, India embodies the meaning of Sidhu - "Follower of the Sidhas". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
